title: ha/dr: multi-AZ failover automation + runbooks-as-code (Helm + Terraform + installer)
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Motivation: Make Private deployments (VPC / on-prem installer) resilient across AZ outages and reduce operational toil during restore drills. This PR implements end-to-end automation for multi-AZ failover and restore drills, adds runbooks-as-code (runnable runbooks in the repo), and makes Helm/Terraform changes required by the installer to reliably perform canary failovers and automated rollbacks.

What I changed (high level):
- Terraform: new module 'ha_dr' that provisions multi-AZ failover resources (route53 failover records, cross-AZ load balancer health checks, S3-backed state for restore metadata). Adds optional 'secondary_az' outputs and a 'promotion' IAM role.
- Helm charts: added hooks and templates to redwood-private-operator chart: pre-failover job, post-failover verification job, adjustable PodDisruptionBudgets, and a 'dr-rollback' hook that can be invoked by the installer to rollback to a pinned chart revision. Introduced charts/values to allow nodeSelector/affinity overrides per-AZ.
- Installer: new CLI command 'redwood-installer dr-run --dr-id <id>' which triggers a coordinated failover/restore drill. The command calls the Terraform module for promotion and creates a Kubernetes Job that runs verification probes. The installer now supports '--dry-run' to generate runbook steps without making changes.
- Runbooks-as-code: added directory 'runbooks/ha-dr' with YAML-defined runbooks that can be executed by the installer or used as documentation. Includes two runbooks: 'multi-az-failover.yaml' and 'restore-drill-checklist.yaml' (both executable via the installer).
- Workflows & CI: added GitHub Actions workflow '.github/workflows/dr-runbook-test.yml' that spins up a lightweight canary cluster (k3s) in CI, deploys the Helm chart, runs the dr-run command in dry-run and simulated-failover modes, and validates the runbook steps succeed.
- Tests & tooling: integration test harness updates in 'test/e2e/dr' with a deterministic failure injector and end-to-end assertions.

Why this matters: Operators running private deployments can now codify DR runbooks, run automated restore drills, and perform failovers with fewer manual steps. The automation reduces mean time to recover (MTTR) and makes drills repeatable for audits.

Review summary (thread):
- Samir: "Can we make the terraform module idempotent for repeated promotions? Also need explicit notes on IAM permissions required for the promotion role."
- Aisha (author): "Addressed in terraform/main.tf: promotion role is conditional and uses a 'promotion_lock' S3 state key to avoid concurrent promotions. Updated README with IAM snippet."
- Evan: "We should not store sensitive promotion metadata in plain S3. Please add KMS encryption and a clear rotate path for the key."
- Aisha: "Added kms_key_id optional input and encrypted the S3 bucket. Added automation docs for key rotation in docs/operational/runbooks/ha-dr.md."
- Rina: "CI k3s job was flaky on first run; can you increase timeouts and make the harness more deterministic? Also request stronger assertions for post-failover readiness (not just HTTP 200)."
- Aisha: "Increased timeouts, added probe retries with exponential backoff, and added post-failover KV-store sanity checks. Ran CI 3x locally; harness stable."
- Marta: "Security review: ensure secrets used by dr jobs are ephemeral and not committed to the repo. Replace example secrets with placeholders in runbooks."
- Aisha: "Replaced all sample secrets with 'REDACTED' placeholders and added note in runbooks to wire secrets via secret manager. Installer will read from KMS/HSM in private installs; doc updated to reflect that."
- Evan (approved): "LGTM after minor nits fixed."
- Samir (approved): "Approving; this is required for upcoming customer audit."

CI and rollout notes: the first CI run revealed a flake in the k3s network setup (timeout). Fixed by increasing cluster bootstrap timeout and adding deterministic port assignment. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, terraform fmt, helm lint, e2e/dr).

Migration and upgrade notes: The Helm chart introduces new CRD fields and a migration hook that will create necessary PDBs and adjust affinity during upgrade. This PR includes a 'pre-upgrade' check that will fail the upgrade if there are not enough nodes in remaining AZs (safe-guard). Operators should run 'redwood-installer preflight --dr-check' before applying the upgrade.

Rollback strategy: The 'dr-rollback' Helm hook will revert to the previous chart revision and run a post-rollback verification job. The installer supports 'redwood-installer dr-rollback --dr-id <id>' for automated rollback paths.

Runbook execution: Runbooks are executable by the installer or via the GitHub Actions workflow. Each runbook step includes a human-readable description, an automation 'action' (terraform apply, helm upgrade, k8s job), timeouts, and expected validation checks.

Backwards compatibility: Changes are opt-in. Terraform module defaults to no-auto-promotion. Helm changes are backwards-compatible when values.dr.enabled=false. The installer command is additive and does not change default install behavior.

Release notes: Added HA/DR automation for private installer: terraform module for promotion, Helm hooks for failover/rollback, executable runbooks-as-code, and CI harness for restore drills.
